record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: Let O(n, n, q) = {π_0, …, π_{q^n}} be a pseudo-oval in PG(3n − 1, q). For fixed i, the paper defines an (n − 1)-spread S_i of a skew PG(2n − 1, q) using the tangent space τ_i and the intersections <π_i, π_j> ∩ PG(2n − 1, q). In the even-q case, it also defines an (n − 1)-spread S using the nucleus η and the intersections PG(2n − 1, q) ∩ <η, π_j>. What structural consequences follow when, in the situation described by the source, the spread S, respectively S_i, is regular?

evidence.quote: 5. What can be said if q is even and the (n − 1)-spread S, respectively Si, defined at the beginning of this section, is regular?

Let PG(2n − 1, q) ⊂ PG(3n − 1, q) be skew to πi, i ∈ {0, 1,...,qn}. Further, let τi∩PG(2n−1, q) = ξi,<πi, πj > ∩PG(2n−1, q) = ξj , j = i. Then {ξ0, ξ1,...,ξqn } = Si is an (n − 1)-spread of PG(2n − 1, q). Now let q be even and let η be the nucleus of O(n, n, q). Let PG(2n − 1, q) be skew to η. If ζj = PG(2n − 1, q)∩ < η, πj >, then {ζ0, ζ1,...,ζqn } = S is an (n − 1)-spread of PG(2n − 1, q).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power and n a positive integer. A pseudo-oval of PG(3n−1, q) is a set
  O(n, n, q) = {π_0, π_1, …, π_{q^n}}
of q^n + 1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(3n−1, q) such that any three of them span PG(3n−1, q). For each i there is a unique (3n−1−n)=(2n−1)-dimensional subspace τ_i, called the tangent space at π_i, that contains π_i and meets every other π_j (j ≠ i) trivially in the sense required by the pseudo-oval (equivalently, the unique (2n−1)-space through π_i skew to all π_j for j ≠ i in the appropriate dual sense). When q is even, the tangent spaces τ_0, …, τ_{q^n} all share a common (n−1)-dimensional subspace η, called the nucleus of O(n, n, q).

Fix a (2n−1)-dimensional subspace PG(2n−1, q) of PG(3n−1, q) that is skew to π_i (resp. skew to η). Define
  S_i = {ξ_i, ξ_0, ξ_1, …, ξ_{q^n}} \ {ξ_i-duplicate},
where ξ_i = τ_i ∩ PG(2n−1, q) and ξ_j = ⟨π_i, π_j⟩ ∩ PG(2n−1, q) for j ≠ i; this is an (n−1)-spread of PG(2n−1, q).
When q is even, define analogously
  S = {ζ_0, ζ_1, …, ζ_{q^n}}, where ζ_j = PG(2n−1, q) ∩ ⟨η, π_j⟩;
this is also an (n−1)-spread of PG(2n−1, q).

Recall that an (n−1)-spread of PG(2n−1, q) is called regular (Desarguesian) if for any three of its elements the unique regulus they determine is contained in the spread; equivalently, the spread arises from the field-reduction of a 1-spread of PG(1, q^n).

Problem. Assume q is even. Determine the structural consequences for the pseudo-oval O(n, n, q) (and for the associated translation generalized quadrangle T(O)) under each of the following hypotheses:
 (a) the (n−1)-spread S defined via the nucleus η is regular;
 (b) for some (equivalently, every) i, the (n−1)-spread S_i defined via the tangent space τ_i is regular.
In particular, does regularity of S (resp. S_i) force O(n, n, q) to be a pseudo-conic (i.e., to arise from field reduction of a conic in PG(2, q^n)), and consequently force T(O) to be isomorphic to the classical generalized quadrangle Q(4, q^n)?
artifact.category_tag: Finite incidence geometry: pseudo-ovals and spreads
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Lavrauw–Popiel and collaborators, including a 2024 Designs, Codes and Cryptography paper) has classified pseudo-ovals and translation generalized quadrangles of small order and addressed cases where one associated plane is Desarguesian, but a general structural answer to the regularity question for S and S_i in even characteristic does not appear in the located sources. The status of the problem in full generality is not clearly resolved by the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Classifying pseudo-ovals, translation generalized quadrangles, and elation Laguerre planes of small order
status_evidence.snippet: Provides classification results for pseudo-ovals in PG(3n-1,q) for small n, and TGQs of order ≤ 64; partial results assuming one associated plane is Desarguesian.
status_evidence.claim: Active classification work exists but does not give a complete general answer to the regular-spread question.

status_evidence.title: On eggs and translation generalised quadrangles (Lavrauw)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys eggs/pseudo-ovals, nucleus in even characteristic, and associated spreads, listing structural questions tied to regularity.
status_evidence.claim: The regularity-of-associated-spread question is a recognized structural problem in the area.
